title: The Principle of Uncertainty in Quantum Mechanics
text:
Heisenberg's uncertainty principle is a fundamental concept in quantum mechanics stating that certain pairs of physical properties, like position and momentum, cannot be simultaneously known with perfect accuracy. The more precisely one measurement determines one variable, the less accurately another conjugate variable can be determined, and vice versa.

This limit is not due to limitations of measurement equipment but is an inherent property of nature itself at the quantum scale. It suggests that reality, when viewed through this lens, does not allow for perfect determinism regarding all measurable pairs of observables.
